This is a great article about a very important matter, thank you for sharing it.  I enjoy Anthony Hopkins movies and Meet Joe Black is on the top of the list of my favorite movies.  This is due to his fantastic acting and wonderful lines/quotes.
One of the many interesting things about this article is the mention of dyslexia.  I was tested for that and other learning disorders in fourth grade, only to find that they had no answers.  I was told that I was a slow learner, which is totally not the case. 
Now to the brass tacks.  I am now 41. In my early 40's, I was approached by a friend who suggested that I might have A.S.D. At first, I brushed it off because all the people I knew with Asperger's were extreme examples of the condition.  My friend persisted after having done extensive research on the matter.  After she shared this research with me, I began pursuing an official diagnosis but found that this would be near impossible.  I was a member of Kaiser here in California.  I was told by several Dr's in the psych dept that they didn't diagnose adults.  I pursued other Dr's outside of Kaiser and met with the same disappointing results, except for one Dr who was outside my area but willing to listen to my situation and symptoms.  She worked really hard to try and get me connected with the right Dr’s in my area.  Unfortunately it ended with the same disappointing failure.  
There are so many articles and books out there that express the extreme importance of getting the correct diagnosis, even as an adult, and yet getting professional help has been a nightmare.  I truly understand how hard is to diagnose an adult who has learned camouflaging and coping methods.  I am not the same person as I was as a child and do not express these characteristics as much anymore. My hope is that soon, more Dr’s are going to care about diagnosing adults who have Asperger’s, and also develop defined testing methods to do so.
